If the violation is not so corrected, the licensing officer may physically seal that portion of the licensed premises causing the violation and order the discontinuance of use thereof until the violation has been corrected and the seal removed by the licensing officer. The licensing officer shall affix to the sealed premises a conspicuous sign labeled "unclean" or "unsafe" as the case may be.
(Ord. No. 230, § 33, 10-3-2005)
338:
A licensed premises or any party thereof may be abated as a sanitary nuisance.
(Ord. No. 230, § 34, 10-3-2005)
341:
The following words, terms, or phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meaning ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Amusement game room means any location where one or more bona fide coin-operated amusement machines are operated that permit non-cash redemption as provided in O.C.G.A. § 16-12-35(d)(1)(B) or (C), or a combination thereof. Amusement game room shall not mean a location where all bona fide coin-operated amusement machines therein offer only free replays, and the number of machines do not exceed six.
Bona fide coin-operated amusement machine means the same as this term is defined in O.C.G.A. § 50-27-70(2) and any applicable regulations of the state.
Location means a business within the city that has complied with the provisions of the ordinances of the city relating to occupation taxes and business licenses.
(Ord. No. 275, § I, 3-2-2009; Ord. No. 2010-315, § 1, 5-3-2010)
343:
Every amusement game room in the city shall comply with the proximity provisions for businesses licensed to sell alcohol in the city.
(Ord. No. 275, § III, 3-2-2009)
344:
No amusement game room in the city shall offer to the public more than six bona fide coin-operated amusement machines offering non-cash redemption in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 16-12-35(d)(1)(B), (C), or both at the same location. After a hearing, the mayor and council may, after consideration of the nature and character of the business, waive the application of this provision to an individual location.
(Ord. No. 275, § IV, 3-2-2009)
345:
No amusement game room in the city shall be open except during the hours of 9:00 a.m. through 11:00 p.m. Monday through Saturday. All amusement game rooms in the city shall be closed on Sunday.
(Ord. No. 275, § V, 3-2-2009)
346:
Every amusement game room shall keep records available for inspection by city officials that set out separately annual gross receipts for the amusement games and the other products and services sold at the location. Income from the amusement game or games shall not constitute more than 50 percent of the income from the location. Compliance with this section requires both the availability of records for inspection and compliance with the 50 percent income requirement.
(Ord. No. 275, § VI, 3-2-2009)
347:
(a) Every amusement game room shall post a conspicuous sign with the following similar words:
Georgia law prohibits giving or receipt of any money for winning a game or games on an amusement machine; giving or receipt of money for free replays won on an amusement machine; giving or receipt of money for ay merchandise, prize, toy, gift certificate, or novelty won on an amusement machine; or awarding any merchandise, prize, toy, gift certificate, or novelty of a value exceeding $5.00 for a single play of an amusement machine.
(b) Every amusement game room shall post the license issued by the city conspicuously and permanently.
(c) The owner or operator of each amusement game room shall inform every employee of the acts and omissions prohibited by O.C.G.A. § 16-12-35, and by this article, and of the penalties for violation O.C.G.A. § 16-12-35 and this article.
(Ord. No. 275, § VII, 3-2-2009)
348:
Bona fide coin-operated amusement machines may be used in an amusement game room within the city only if the machines are owned by a person who holds a valid master license in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 50-27-71, and each machine offered to the public for play has a valid permit sticker in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 50-27-78. The city official in charge of issuing business licenses shall notify the state commissioner of revenue of any observed violation of O.C.G.A. § 50-27-71 or 50-27-78.
(Ord. No. 275, § VIII, 3-2-2009)
349:
(a) In addition to penalties set out in the O.C.G.A. provisions for failure to comply with the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 16-12-35 (a) through (i), the owner or operator of an amusement game room, after conviction in a court of competent jurisdiction, and a hearing before the mayor and council, may be subject to the following penalties:
(1) First offense: suspension for not more than six months of the owner or operator's license for offering any amusement game at the location where the violation occurred.
(2) Second offense: suspension for not more than 12 months of the owner or operator's license for offering any amusement game at the location where the violation occurred.
(3) Third offense: suspension or permanent revocation of the owner or operator's license for offering any amusement game in the location where the violation occurred, and suspension of other permits and licenses granted by the city for not more than six months.
(b) Penalties for violation of the provisions of section 10-78, 10-79, 10-80, 10-82, or 10-83 by the owner or operator of an amusement game room, after conviction by the municipal court of the city, are as follows:
(1) First offense: fine not to exceed $500.00 for each violation.
(2) Second offense: fine not to exceed $750.00 for each violation, suspension of the owner or operator's license for offering any amusement game at the location for not more than three months, or both.
(3) Third offense: fine not to exceed $1,000.00 for each violation, suspension or permanent revocation of the owner or operator's license for offering any amusement game at the location, or suspension of other permits and licenses granted by the city for not more than six months, in any combination of these penalties.
(c) The fines listed in the penalties for violation of this article may be imposed by the judge of the municipal court of the city. Suspension or revocation of the owner or operator's license for offering any amusement game at the location where the violation occurred, and suspension of other permits and licenses granted by the city may be imposed by the mayor and council after a hearing.
(d) Offering one or more bona fide coin-operated amusement games in violation of an order suspending or revoking the license for offering of any amusement game at the location is punishable, after conviction in the municipal court of the city, by a fine not to exceed $1,000.00, imprisonment not to exceed 30 days, or both such fine and imprisonment.
(Ord. No. 275, § IX, 3-2-2009)
350:
The municipal court of the city is authorized impose the following penalties on any person convicted of receiving money as a reward for the successful play or winning of any bona fide coin-operated amusement machine from any person owning or possessing such bona fide coin operated amusement machine or any person employed by or acting on behalf of a person owning or possessing a bona fide coin-operated amusement machine:
(1) First offense: fine not to exceed $250.00 for each violation.
(2) Second and subsequent offenses: fine not to exceed $500.00 for each violation.
(Ord. No. 275, § X, 3-2-2009)
353:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning.
Solicitation activities shall mean the practices of solicitors as listed in the definition of the term "solicitor" in this section.
Solicitor shall mean any person, corporation, limited liability company, partnership, association, joint-stock company, trust or unincorporated organization which, through door-to-door solicitation, engages in the practice of:
(1) Selling or taking orders for or offering to sell or take orders for goods, merchandise, wares, or other items of value for further delivery, or services to be performed in the future, for commercial purposes; or
(2) Requesting contributions of funds, property, or anything of value, or the pledge of any type of future donation, or selling or offering for sale any type or property, including, but not limited to, goods, tickets, books, and pamphlets, for political, charitable, religious, or other noncommercial purposes.
(Ord. No. 2010-310, § 1, 1-27-2010)
354:
It shall be unlawful for any solicitor to engage in solicitation activities in the city without first obtaining a permit from the city.
(Ord. No. 2010-310, § 2, 1-27-2010)
355:
The following solicitors are exempt from the provisions of this article pertaining to obtaining a permit, paying a fee, obtaining an identification badge, and posting a bond;
(1) Minors under the age of 18 years engaged in the solicitation of donations or the sale of any type of property for the purpose of financing extracurricular social, athletic, artistic, scientific, or cultural programs, provided such solicitation activities shall have been approved by the principal of the school sponsoring such social, athletic, artistic, scientific or cultural programs.
(2) Political candidates engaged in the solicitation of campaign contributions, provided that, at the time of such solicitation, each such candidate has formally qualified and is seeking election to a local, state or national elective office.
(3) Non-profit, tax exempt, charitable organization and churches.
(Ord. No. 2010-310, § 3, 1-27-2010)
357:
Each solicitor applying for a permit under this section shall pay the city clerk a permit fee , plus a fee for each individual engaging in door-to-door solicitation on behalf of the solicitor to cover the cost of the identification badge and administration. A solicitor's permit shall be valid for the period of time requested in solicitor's application up to 20 days.
(Ord. No. 2010-310, § 5, 1-27-2010)
358:
(a) Upon applicant's fulfillment of the above requirements, and subject to compliance with this article, the city clerk or the designee shall issue to the applicant a solicitor's permit. No permit shall be issued to any solicitor convicted of a violation of any provision of this article, or whose solicitor's permit has previously been suspended or revoked. No individual convicted of a violation of any provision of this article shall thereafter be permitted to engage in door-to-door solicitation within the city.
(b) Any permit issued hereunder shall be personal to the applicant and shall not be assigned or transferred to any other person, entity, or association. Any such attempt at assignment or transfer shall render the permit void.
(c) In addition to the permit, the city shall issue an identification badge to every individual engaging in door-to-door solicitation on behalf of the solicitor. Such persons shall wear their badges in such a way that the badges may be easily read while doing business. If a badge becomes damaged or obscured, the solicitor shall return it to the city and receive another badge upon payment of the applicable fee. Identification badges shall only be used by the person to whom they were issued and may not be transferred to any other person.
(Ord. No. 2010-310, § 6, 1-27-2010)
359:
The following regulations shall apply to solicitors engaged in solicitation activities in the city:
(1) Solicitation activities shall only be conducted between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. eastern time.
(2) Solicitation activities shall not be conducted in defiance of any notice exhibited by a residence or business indicating that solicitors are not welcome or not invited. In addition, the city clerk shall maintain a list of addresses of residents and businesses which have notified the city that solicitors are not welcome or not invited to their residence or business. Solicitation activities shall not be conducted at these residences or businesses. Any solicitor may obtain a copy of this list upon reimbursing the city for photocopying expenses.
(Ord. No. 2010-310, § 7, 1-27-2010)
360:
(a) Any permit issued under this article may be suspended or revoked for any of the following reasons:
(1) Fraud or misrepresentation in the application for a permit;
(2) Fraud or misrepresentation in the course of conducting solicitation activities;
(3) Conducting solicitation activities contrary to the conditions of the permit; or
(4) Conducting solicitation activities in such a manner as to create a public nuisance or constitute a danger to the public health, safety, or welfare.
(b) Upon suspension or revocation, the city shall deliver written notice to the permit holder stating the action taken and the reason supporting such action. The written notice shall be delivered to the address set forth in the permit holder's application.
(Ord. No. 2010-310, § 8, 1-27-2010)
361:
Solicitors that are denied solicitor's permits or solicitors whose permits have been suspended or revoked may appeal such denial, suspension or revocation by filing a written notice of appeal with the city clerk. The appeal must be filed within ten days of the date of the notice denial, suspension or revocation. The mayor and council shall hear and determine the appeal at its next regularly scheduled meeting and the decision of the mayor and council shall be final.
(Ord. No. 2010-310, § 9, 1-27-2010)
362:
In addition to the suspension and revocation penalties provided for herein, any solicitor or individual engaged in door-to-door solicitation who is found to be in violation of any provision of this article shall be subject to a civil fine according to section 1-4.
(Ord. No. 2010-310, § 10, 1-27-2010)
365:
The purpose of this article is to allow for the licensing and regulation of food trucks operating within the city limits.
(Ord. No. 2021-399, § a, 10-8-2021)
366:
If any provisions of the food truck regulations are found to be in conflict with any other provision or requirement of any other applicable governmental law, ordinance, resolution, rule, or other governmental regulation of any kind, the more restrictive rule or standard shall take precedence.
(Ord. No. 2021-399, § b, 10-8-2021)
367:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Food means a raw, cooked, or processed edible substance, ice cream, ice, beverage, or ingredient used or intended for use or for sale in whole or in part, for human consumption.
Food truck means a licensed, readily movable or motorized wheeled vehicle or trailer, which is temporarily stored on a premise where food items are sold to the general public. The term "food truck" includes vehicles and equipment defined as "mobile food service unit" and/or "extended food service unit" contained and amended in Rules of Department of Public Health, Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. R. 511-6-1-.01 and 511-6-1-.08.
(Ord. No. 2021-399, § c, 10-8-2021)
368:
(a) Prior to an application for a license to operate a food truck in the city, the food truck vendor shall first submit for inspection and be approved by the county health department or by the state department of agriculture if selling commercially packaged food.
(b) No person shall operate a food truck within the corporate limits of the city without first obtaining the proper licenses and/or permits from the state, county, and city. Food truck operators shall at all times comply with the provisions of this article and all other applicable local, state and federal laws, regulations or rules. The food truck vendor, being a business located in the city, must obtain a business license from the city.
(c) The food truck vendor shall obtain and display the county health department-issued state department of public health mobile food service permit at all times during its hours of operations. The food truck vendor shall provide a copy of the mobile food service permit to the city manager prior to beginning operations.
(d) The food truck vendor shall obtain written authorization from the property owner or registered agent of the property for food vending. Such written authorization must be maintained and accessible in the truck at all times during the hours of operations;
(e) Prior to beginning operations, the food truck vendor shall make available the operating food truck for inspection by the building and codes department or designee and the county fire rescue. In order to obtain a license, the food truck vendor shall provide proof that the truck has been inspected by the building and codes department and the county fire rescue and that the truck is in compliance with the National Fire Protection Association and state fire codes.
(f) Food truck vendors shall comply with all city ordinances and city, county, and state retail sales tax regulations.
(Ord. No. 2021-399, § d, 10-8-2021)
370:
No food truck shall operate in public space between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m.
(Ord. No. 2021-399, § f, 10-8-2021)
371:
(a) Temporary connections to potable water are prohibited. All plumbing and electrical connections shall be in accordance with the building code.
(b) Grease is to be disposed of in recyclable grease container at an existing restaurant or commissary (not in sewers, dumpsters, or storm drains or at any residence or other property). A written agreement with an existing restaurant or commissary must be submitted to the city manager prior to beginning operations.
(c) Grey water to be disposed of in the sanitary sewer at an existing restaurant or commissary (no open dumping or into storm drains, sewer clean outs, or any location that does not have an approved grease interceptor) pursuant to city engineering department regulations. A written agreement with an existing restaurant or commissary must be submitted to the city manager prior to beginning operations.
(d) Food trucks must comply with the county fire rescue mobile food vendor fire safety specifications and practices. The county fire rescue will inspect for compliance before a business license will be issued.
(Ord. No. 2021-399, § g, 10-8-2021)
372:
(a) The food truck vendor shall not operate the food truck as a drive-in window.
(b) The noise level or gas fumes from the food truck motor and generator or any other source must comply with the noise ordinance, and they shall not interfere with the health and safety of surrounding businesses, gatherings or public places.
(c) No vehicle using sound equipment or other method of attracting customers shall operate such equipment before 9:00 a.m. or after 8:00 p.m. daily or between the hours of 9:30 a.m. and 12:00 noon on Sundays. Furthermore, such equipment shall not be operated within one block of a church, or within one block of an existing restaurant, between the hours of 9:30 a.m. and 12:00 noon on Sundays.
(d) A covered trash receptacle may be required for the customers by the city sanitation department; the city shall charge a fee in an amount to be determined by mayor and council from time to time per day for one covered trash receptacle. The food truck vendor and property owner shall be responsible for daily cleanup and proper disposal of litter in accordance with city solid waste ordinance. For the wellbeing of public health and safety the city manager may require additional trash receptacles before or after any food truck operating permit is or has been issued. No excess liquid waste consumable and non-consumable products shall be placed in the trash receptacle from the food truck at any time.
(e) If the food truck is proposed to operate after dark, the food truck vendor shall provide a lighting plan which includes use of shielded fixtures and shall not include spotlights. Illumination shall be designed and installed in a manner that minimizes upward light pollution. A combination of shielding, screening, and directing the lighting away from areas beyond the vehicle sign, together with the use of landscaping, if available, to soften the impact of reflected light, shall be used.
(f) No signage shall be allowed other than:
(1) Signs permanently attached to the motor vehicle; or
(2) A portable, non-internally illuminated menu sign no more than six square feet in display area and no more than four feet in height that is placed on the ground in the customer waiting area.
(Ord. No. 2021-399, § h, 10-8-2021)
373:
(a) Food truck vendors may apply to operate in city parks and other city property by submitting a request to the city manager's office. Any request must include proof that the regulations set forth in this article have been met. The city manager, or his designee, shall review each application and approve or reject the same.
(b) A food truck vendor may operate in city parks and other city property, subject to such terms and conditions as the said city manager may from time to time promulgate in writing, which may include terms as to insurance, clean-up fees, deposits, security personnel, limits on the number of guests and other matters as said city manager may require.
(c) This section shall only serve to allow the operation of a food truck on public property under the specific circumstances set forth herein. Nothing in this section shall release a food truck vendor from the location requirements set forth in section 10-149 or any other regulation or requirement set forth in this article.
(Ord. No. 2021-399, § i, 10-8-2021)
374:
Any person violating any of the provisions of this section shall be guilty of a violation of this article and on conviction thereof in the municipal court shall be punished according to section 1-4.
(Ord. No. 2021-399, § j, 10-8-2021)
377:
It is hereby provided for the purposes of this article, the term "junk yard" means a place which for a period of 30 or more days has on its premises two or more motor vehicles which are not in operative condition. Such definition does not include places of business which the city has licensed to operate as motor vehicle repair businesses or garages so long as no individual motor vehicle remains on such premises in a non-operative condition for a period in excess of 30 days.
(1) All junk yards as defined by this article must be surrounded by a chain link fence which is at least seven feet high. Such fence must be located a minimum of 150 feet from the center line of any street, alley or other roadway within the city, and a minimum of 50 feet from adjoining property lines. If a residence is located on the same premises as the junk yard, then all parts of the fence which surrounds such junk yard must be located in the rear of such residence.
(2) All operators of junk yards must plant and maintain shrubbery or trees around the fence which is required to surround the junk yard. Such shrubbery and/or trees must be planted no more than ten feet from the aforementioned fence. Such shrubbery must be property maintained in a living condition. Such shrubbery must be of a type which can reasonably be expected to reach a height of at least five feet within five years and must be planted near enough together so that upon the attainment of the shrubbery and/or trees' maturity that the shrubbery and/or trees will form a continuous hedge type border.
(3) All junk yards must contain a minimum of 100 square feet for each motor vehicle which is not in an operating condition.
(4) Under no condition are motor vehicles located within junk yards to be placed on top of each other.
(5) Unless specifically defined below, words or phrases in this article shall be construed so as to give them the meaning they have in common usage and to give this article its most reasonable application. However, the following specific definitions shall be applied in the interpretation and enforcement of this article:
Enforcement officer means the chief of police or officers of the city police department.
Junk or inoperable motor vehicle means an automobile, motorcycle, motor truck, trailer, semi-trailer, tractor trailer combination, and all other vehicles designed or intended to be operated over the public streets and highways and used as a means of transporting persons or property over the same that are propelled by power, other than muscle power, or parts thereof, that is wrecked, ruined, dismantled, partially dismantled, inoperative, or is abandoned or discarded, or does not have a current license plate and a current tag registration decal.
Owner means an owner, lessee, person in possession of real property or any other individual, association, firm, partnership or corporation having an ownership or possessory interest in real property.
Person means an individual, association, firm, partnership and body politic and corporate and as the same relates to real property shall include both the record title owner of such real property, a tenant thereon, or any other person in possession of such real property.
(6) For the purpose of promoting the health, safety and welfare of the city, every owner of private real property within the city is required to keep his property free and clear of conditions which tend or are likely to breed pests such as rodents or mosquitoes, create a fire or safety hazard that endanger the lives and property of citizens, or which constitute an unsightly or unsanitary condition. In furtherance thereof, the existence of any junk or inoperable motor vehicle on public or private property is hereby declared and shall be deemed a public nuisance.
(7) It shall be unlawful and a violation of this article for any person to leave, place, deposit, discard or dump any junk or inoperable motor vehicle on any public or private real property within the city, except in accordance with this article and the zoning and business regulations of the city.
(8) It shall be unlawful for any person to park, keep, store, leave or permit the parking, storage, or leaving of any junk or inoperable motor vehicle, whether attended or not, on any private real property within the city; except that this section shall not apply to:
a. A junk or inoperable motor vehicle that is located within a completely enclosed building or structure, lawfully on the property, so that the inoperable or unlicensed motor vehicle is not visible from other property or from a public right-of-way;
b. A junk or inoperable motor vehicle that is stored or parked on real property in connection with a business of a licensed motor vehicle sales or service dealer, motor vehicle repair shop, junkyard, or other property of a licensed business operating in a lawful place, other than a residential zone district, operated in a lawful manner, when the keeping or presence of such junk or inoperable motor vehicle is necessary to the operation of the business or when the keeping or presence of such motor vehicle is appropriate because the business is operated as a lawful storage place, repair facility or depositary for junk or inoperable motor vehicles;
c. An inoperable motor vehicle stored on private real property, not enclosed within a building, if the motor vehicle has a currently valid tag registration and license plate affixed thereon and is titled in the name of a person currently residing on the premises.
(9) Whenever it is determined by a city enforcement officer that there exists on any private real property within the city, a junk or inoperable motor vehicle, the owner, tenant, person in possession, or owner's property manager, if known, shall be given written notice to remove and properly disposed of the junk or inoperable motor vehicle within ten business days of the receipt of notice. Where personal service of notice is not possible on an owner residing within the city, notice shall be given by certified U.S. mail, return receipt requested, to the owner as shown upon the most recent tax digest of the county.
(10) Upon the owner's failure to remove and properly disposed of such junk or inoperable motor vehicle, or to cause the proper registration and licensing of the same, within the time permitted by the notice, a city enforcement officer shall cause a citation to be issued to the owner, tenant, or person in possession of the property, for violation of this article.
(11) Any person found in violation of this article shall be subject to a civil penalty of not less than $100.00 and not more than $1,000.00.
(Ord. No. 63, § 3, 8-1-1966; Ord. No. 63(1), § 3, 6-3-2013)
378:
The city shall have the power and right to issue a license for the operation of junk yards. Conditions precedent to the issuance of such license are that the applicant for such license sign a written affidavit to the effect that he has complied with all the requirements of this article in regard to the operation of such junk yard and that said applicant pay a fee of $250.00 for the issuance of such a license and that said applicant furnish any and all other information required by the officials of the city to prove that said applicant has complied with this article. Said license shall be issued for a period of no longer than one year. Such license is renewable yearly with the same conditions precedent to its being re-issued as for its original issuance. Such license is revocable at any time for noncompliance with the above provisions after the operator of the junk yard which is alleged to be operating in violation of this article is given a written notice signed by the mayor that said junk yard is being operated in a manner not in conformity with this article and such operator is given a 30-day period to comply with this article.
(Ord. No. 63, § 4, 8-1-1966; Ord. No. 63(1), § 4, 6-3-2013)
379:
The penalty for operating a junk yard without a license shall be a fine of $25.00 per vehicle per day. Such penalty is to be exacted after notice to the operator of the junk yard he is operating in violation of this article and after such operator is given 30 days to comply with this article, after a hearing before the city judge.
(Ord. No. 63, § 5, 8-1-1966; Ord. No. 63(1), § 5, 6-3-2013)
382:
The following words and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context indicates a different meaning:
Company means the holder of a license to operate a horse-drawn carriage business under the provisions of this article, whether a person, firm, partnership, corporation or entity.
Driver means any person who drives or operates a horse-drawn carriage on the streets of the city for a licensed company.
Driver's permit means the written authority granted by the city for an individual to drive or operate a horse-drawn carriage within the city.
Horse-drawn carriage means any hack or carriage which is operated by being drawn by a horse, mule or other beast of burden, for the transportation for hire of passengers.
License means the right and privilege granted by the city for the operation of a business incorporating the use of one or more horse-drawn carriages within the corporate limits of the city.
Loading zone means a location designated by the city council for the loading and unloading of passengers where a carriage does not remain in excess of ten minutes.
Special event means a prearranged tour to accommodate a one time, nonrecurring special occasion such as a wedding party, celebration, or nonprofit activity.
Stand means a public place alongside the curb of a street or elsewhere which has been designated by the mayor and councilmembers for the parking of carriages and that are reserved exclusively for the use of horse-drawn carriages.
Street means and includes any street, alley, lane, avenue, court or public place in the city.
Veterinarian means a veterinarian licensed in the state who specializes in large animals.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 1, 3-5-2012)
383:
(a) Business license required. No person, firm, corporation or entity shall operate a business involving the use of one or more horse-drawn carriages on the streets of the city unless a license for such business has first been granted by the city. The license shall be effective only for the period of time stated in the license, unless suspended or revoked sooner as provided by ordinance. The following license fee in an amount to be determined by mayor and council from time to time for operating horse carriages inside the city shall be charged:
(1) Individual special event for carriage hire, per event; or
(2) A yearly fee for carriage licensing, which shall be prorated by 50 percent if purchased after June 30.
(b) Forms; renewal. Application for the license shall be made on forms provided by the city clerk. Yearly licenses shall expire on the January 1 which follows the date of issue. License renewals may be granted after filing a new application form with updated application requirements.
(c) Required information. Each horse-drawn carriage company, as a condition for holding a license under the provisions of this article, shall give to the city the name, address, and telephone number of the veterinarian who certifies the health of the horses. The carriage company shall also provide the following information available to the city manager and/or his designee:
(1) Written certification from a veterinarian which states:
a. All immunizations are current.
b. The horse is in good health and able to haul.
c. The maximum weight the horse is able to safely haul.
(2) A picture of the horse and a name or other designation for the horse.
(d) Operating regulations. In addition to the license requirements imposed herein, no license shall be permitted any carriage operator unless the operator complies with the following operating regulations:
(1) No single animal shall pull a carriage holding more than the veterinarian certified weight that a horse can pull.
(2) No animal having open sores or wounds or any disease or ailment shall be permitted to be in service on the streets of the city.
(3) Each draft animal shall have its hooves properly trimmed and shod for street surfaces.
(4) Each animal shall be groomed daily and not have fungus, dandruff, or a dirty coat.
(5) Harnesses shall be properly fitted, maintained, and oiled so that no irritating material will come in direct contact with the animal.
(6) No driver may use more than a light touch of the whip upon any animal, and no driver or other person may forcefully strike an animal or make movements or noise intended to frighten or harm an animal.
(7) No driver shall permit an animal to pull a carriage at a speed faster than a slow trot, except in emergency situations.
(8) No animal shall be subject to any condition or treatment, whether in service or out of service, which will impair the good health and physical condition of that animal.
(9) Adequate water shall be provided to the draft animal while in service.
(10) Prompt veterinary care and services shall be provided to sick horses. Sick horses shall be immediately removed from service.
(11) Horses shall not be worked in extreme weather conditions. Horses will not be operated when the ambient temperature reaches 95 degrees or when the heat index reaches or exceeds 100 degrees.
(12) No animal may be worked for more than eight hours per day. The driver must keep a log of starting and ending times for each animal. The log should be stored and available for inspection on the carriage being pulled.
(e) Inspection. The city manager or his designee shall be empowered to inspect all carriages, stables, stalls and operating facilities of any carriage company without notice and to examine operating practices of any carriage company to ensure continuous compliance with this article.
(f) Noncompliance. Any applicant who refuses or fails to comply with the requirements of this article shall not be issued a license. The foregoing licensing requirements shall be ongoing as requirements for continuous operation.
(g) Other applicable laws. Operators and or agents of the carriage company and passengers shall comply with all city ordinances and state and federal laws which govern the use of horse drawn carriages and the treatment of animals, including horses, mules, or other oxen of burden.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 2, 3-5-2012)
384:
(a) Indemnity for benefit of city. Any horse-drawn carriage company operating under this article shall hold the city, its officers, agents, servants and employees harmless against any and all liability, loss, damages or expense which may accrue to the city by reason of negligence, default or misconduct of the company in connection with the rights granted to such company hereunder. Nothing in this article shall be considered to make the city, its officers, agents, servants or employees liable for damages because of any negligent act or omission or commission by any horse-drawn carriage company, its servants, agents, drivers or other employees, during the operation by the company of a horse-drawn carriage business or service, either with respect to injury to persons or with respect to damage to property which may be sustained.
(b) Insurance for benefit of passengers. Any horse-drawn carriage company desiring a license to do business shall give and maintain a policy of indemnity from an insurance company authorized to do business in the state for each vehicle in use as a horse-drawn carriage. The minimum coverage shall be $100,000.00 for bodily injury to any one person, $300,000.00 for injury to more than one person which is sustained in the same accident, and $25,000.00 for property damage resulting from one accident. The indemnity insurance shall insure to the benefit of any person who shall be injured or who shall sustain damage to property caused by the negligence of a horse-drawn carriage company, its servants or agents.
(c) Blanket policy. Any company or person operating a horse-drawn carriage in the city shall give a separate policy of indemnity insurance for each separate horse-drawn carriage for hire, except where such company or person actually owns or holds legal title to more than one horse-drawn carriage, in which event such company or person may give one policy of indemnity insurance covering all the horse-drawn carriages actually owned. This latter provision, however, shall not apply to any group of persons separately owning horse-drawn carriages who may be jointly operating or doing business under a licensed horse-drawn carriage name.
(d) Notice when voided. Before any policy of insurance required by this article is voided for any cause, nonpayment of premium or otherwise, notice thereof shall be given, in writing, to the city clerk at least five days before the same shall take effect.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 3, 3-5-2012)
385:
(a) Permit required and fee. No person shall operate a horse-drawn carriage for hire upon the streets of the city, and no person who owns or operates a horse-drawn carriage company shall permit a horse-drawn carriage to be driven, and no horse-drawn carriage operating under a horse-drawn carriage company licensed by the city shall be driven at any time for hire, unless the driver of the horse-drawn carriage shall first have obtained and shall have then in force a horse-drawn carriage driver's permit issued under the provisions of this article. An administrative fee in an amount to be determined by mayor and council from time to time must be submitted with the application.
(b) Application. Any person desiring a permit required by this article shall submit to the city clerk the following information:
(1) City provided application form with the following attached.
(2) Copy of current valid motor vehicle operator's license.
(3) Copy of criminal history.
(4) Copy of driver's history.
(5) Written certification from the carriage licensee that the carriage driver is fully competent, to drive a horse drawn carriage. The competency certification must be notarized by a public notary licensed in the state.
(6) An executed and notarized SAVE affidavit in the form approved by the state.
(c) Qualifications of applicant. An applicant for a driver's permit under this article must not be less than 18 years of age, with no physical infirmities which might make the applicant an unsafe or unsatisfactory horse-drawn carriage driver. No drivers permit shall be issued to any person who has been convicted of operating a motor vehicle under the influence of intoxicating beverages or drugs within two years prior to the date of the application for such permit or have been convicted of reckless driving within one year prior to the date of the application for such permit, or been convicted of any of these offenses three or more times within three years prior to the date of application for such permit. Nor shall a permit be issued to an applicant who within three years prior to the date of the application for such permit have been convicted of, been on probation, parole, or served time on a sentence for a felony. The applicant shall be a citizen of the United States or an alien admitted for permanent residence or who has otherwise been granted employment authorization by the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services.
(d) Permit not transferable. Any horse-drawn carriage driver's permit issued under this article is not transferable and is to be used solely by the person to whom it is issued.
(e) Duration of permit; renewals. A horse-drawn carriage driver's permit shall expire at the end of the calendar year in which it was issued and may be renewed unless the permit for the preceding period has been revoked or is under suspension.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 4, 3-5-2012)
386:
Every horse-drawn carriage operated on the streets of the city shall be maintained in a safe mechanical condition, with all safety equipment remaining intact and operative at all times when the horse-drawn carriage is in service.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 5, 3-5-2012)
387:
Each vehicle operating under this article shall be kept painted and in a clean and sanitary condition, free of litter and debris and at all times suitable for public transportation of passengers.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 6, 3-5-2012)
388:
The city manager or the chief of police or their respective designees shall have the authority to remove from operation on the streets of the city any vehicle used as a horse-drawn carriage which is in violation of this article and to prohibit operation of the horse-drawn carriage until all deficiencies have been corrected. An order to remove a vehicle from the streets shall be effective immediately but may be appealed to the city council as provided in section 10-218.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 7, 3-5-2012)
389:
(a) No parking. No parking of a horse-drawn carriage shall be permitted in the corporate limits of the city except at such stands as may be established by the mayor and council upon the recommendation of the city manager, which parking stands shall be designated by signs. Whenever any stand is established, the stand may be used by horse-drawn carriages upon a rotation basis of first come, first served.
(b) Stand maintenance. Drivers of horse-drawn vehicles operated under this article shall maintain stands in a sanitary condition at all times. Any failure on the part of the driver or drivers to conform to the requirements of this section shall be unlawful and shall subject the driver to the penalties provided herein.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 8, 3-5-2012)
390:
(a) Passengers may be loaded or discharged only in designated loading zones. Carriages may remain in a loading zone only while loading or discharging passengers or while waiting to load passengers. However, no carriage may remain in a loading zone for more than ten minutes without providing water to the horse.
(b) The following are designated as loading zones:
(1) Carriage stands designated by the city manager or his designee.
(2) Location on private property (i.e., outside of the road right-of-way) or locations designated on public property for prearranged tours, special events, and point to point transportation.
(3) Locations on streets adjacent to homes, restaurants, hotels, churches, and other establishments for prearranged tours, special events, or point to point transportation for persons departing from or arriving at those establishments, providing that there is no off-street parking otherwise available and that the carriage is parked outside any travel lane.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 9, 3-5-2012)
391:
It shall be unlawful for any driver of any horse-drawn carriage to leave the vehicle unattended, or the immediate premises thereof, while the vehicle is parked in a horse-drawn carriage stand or otherwise in service.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 10, 3-5-2012)
392:
It shall be unlawful for any person to solicit passengers verbally or by gesture, directly or indirectly, at any horse-drawn carriage stand or upon the streets of the city.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 11, 3-5-2012)
393:
No driver shall permit more persons to be carried in a horse-drawn carriage as passengers than the rated seating capacity of his horse-drawn carriage. A child in arms shall not be counted as a passenger.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 12, 3-5-2012)
394:
No driver shall refuse or neglect to convey any orderly persons, upon request, unless previously engaged or unable or forbidden by the provisions of this article to do so.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 13, 3-5-2012)
395:
No driver shall collect fares, make change, or take on or discharge passengers while his horse-drawn carriage is in motion.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 14, 3-5-2012)
396:
(a) No horse-drawn carriage shall be operated on city streets between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 8:30 a.m. on any day.
(b) Hours of operation may be altered for special events only upon approval of the city council.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 15, 3-5-2012)
397:
All carriage routes, including those for point to point special hires, must be approved by the chief of police and be adhered to at all times.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 16, 3-5-2012)
398:
(a) Manure and urine must be immediately treated with a chemical deodorizing solution, and manure must be removed immediately from the street by the carriage operator. Horse diapers, which prevent excrement from being deposited on the street surface will be used. All diapers must be maintained and free of defects.
(b) The carriage operator is responsible for the disposal of any and all waste product that is created by the operation of his business. Disposal in pet waste containers or trash cans located throughout the city is prohibited.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 17, 3-5-2012)
399:
The operation of horse-drawn vehicles within the city shall be subject to vehicle and traffic provisions of this article and to the traffic laws of the state. No driver shall permit an animal to pull a carriage at a speed faster than a slow trot, except in emergency situations. Stopping along a tour route by a driver for purposes other than allowing for traffic or gaining control of the horse is prohibited. Carriages must be kept moving at all times except as required by traffic regulations or where particular exigencies reasonably require it.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 18, 3-5-2012)
400:
The city manager or the chief of police or their respective designees shall have the authority to suspend a driver's permit or horse-drawn carriage license, as the case may be, for up to 60 days for the following reasons:
(1) Making any false statement in the application for the person of the company.
(2) Operating a horse-drawn carriage in violation of any provision of this article or state law.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 19, 3-5-2012)
401:
In the event that any driver or company holding a license or permit under this article at any time ceases to meet the qualifications described in this article, or fails to correct satisfactorily any false statement made in the application for the license or permit, or to cure any violation of this article that is subject to cure within the suspended period, or in the case of a driver, incurs two traffic violations while in control of the horse-drawn carriage, the city manager shall be empowered to revoke permanently the license or permit.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 20, 3-5-2012)
402:
It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, corporation or entity to operate a horse-drawn carriage for hire for the carrying of passengers within the city, and for any person holding a driver's permit to drive a horse-drawn carriage within the city during any period in which such license or permit is suspended or revoked.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 21, 3-5-2012)
403:
Appeals of decisions of the city manager or the chief of police, or their respective designees, with respect to the suspension or revocation of a horse-drawn carriage license or driver's permit shall be conducted as follows: An appeal to the mayor and council from a ruling of the city manager or the chief of police shall be made within 30 days of the ruling. The appellant shall be informed within ten days of the ruling in writing of the reasons for the decision of the city manager or chief of police. The appellant shall have the right to present evidence, examine the evidence of the appellee, and to cross examine. The appellant shall have the right to be represented by counsel.
(Ord. No. 2012-328, § 22, 3-5-2012)
406:
There is hereby levied for each year an annual license fee upon each insurer doing business within the city in an amount to be determined by the mayor and council from time to time. For each separate business location in excess of one not covered by section 10-246, which is operating on behalf of such insurers within the city, there is hereby levied a license fee in an amount to be determined by mayor and council from time to time. For the purposes of this article, the term "insurer" means a company which is authorized to transact business in any of the classes of insurance designated in O.C.G.A. § 33-3-5.
(Ord. No. 181, § 1, 11-7-1994)
407:
For each separate business location, not otherwise subject to a license fee hereunder, operated and maintained by a business organization which is engaged in the business of lending money or transacting sales involving term financing and in connection with such loans or sales offers, solicits or takes application for insurance through a licensed agent of an insurer for insurance, said insurer shall pay an additional license fee in an amount to be determined by mayor and council from time to time per location for each year.
(Ord. No. 181, § 2, 11-7-1994)
408:
There is hereby levied for each year an annual license fee upon independent agencies and brokers for each separate business location from which an insurance business is conducted and which is not subject to the company license fee imposed by section 10-245 in an amount to be determined by the mayor and council from time to time for each such location within the city.
(Ord. No. 181, § 3, 11-7-1994)
409:
There is hereby levied for each year an annual tax based solely upon gross direct premiums upon each insurer writing life, accident and sickness insurance within the state in an amount equal to one percent of the gross direct premiums received during the preceding calendar year in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 33-8-8.1. Gross direct premiums as used in this section shall mean gross direct premiums as used in O.C.G.A. § 33-8-4. The premium tax levied by this section is in addition to the license fee imposed by section 10-245.
(Ord. No. 181, § 4, 11-7-1994)
410:
There is hereby levied for each year an annual tax based solely upon gross direct premiums upon each insurer, other than an insurer transacting business in the class of insurance designated in O.C.G.A. § 33-3-5(1), doing business within the state in an amount equal to 2.5 percent of the gross direct premiums received during the preceding calendar year in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 33-8-8.2. Gross direct premiums as used in this section shall mean gross direct premiums as used in O.C.G.A. § 33-8-4. The premium tax levied by this section is in addition to the license fees imposed by section 10-245.
(Ord. No. 181, § 5, 11-7-1994)
411:
License fees imposed in sections 10-245 and 10-246 shall be due and payable on the first day of each year.
(Ord. No. 181, § 4, 11-7-1994)
414:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Employee means any person working for an owner or pawnbroker, or any owner pawnbroker who, in the performance of duties or the management of the business affairs of a pawnshop, comes into substantial contact with members of the public, or is employed on a part-time or full-time basis, either with or without remuneration, by a pawnshop.
Pawn orpledge means a bailment of personal property as security for any debt or engagement, redeemable upon certain terms and with the implied power of sale on default.
Pawnbroker means any person, whether an owner or not, who works in a pawnshop on a regular basis and in a managerial capacity whereby the person has charge of the business or operations of the pawnshop. Pawnbroker includes any person whose business or occupation it is to take or receive, by way of pledge, pawn or exchange, any goods, wares or merchandise or any kind of personal property whatever, as security for the repayment of money lent thereon.
Pawnshop means any business wherein a substantial part thereof is to take or receive, by way of pledge, pawn or exchange, any goods, wares, merchandise or any kind of personal property as security for the repayment of money lent thereon.
(Ord. No. 2015-370, § 1, 9-8-2015)
415:
It shall be unlawful for any person or entity to act as a pawnbroker or to operate a pawnshop in the city without a current pawnbroker permit. It shall be unlawful for any pawnbroker or pawnshop to operate in violation of this article.
(Ord. No. 2015-370, § 2, 9-8-2015)
416:
(a) Before operating a pawnshop, the owner must first file an application with the city manager for a pawnbroker permit and obtain the approval of the permit by the mayor and council. Failure of the mayor and council to approve or disapprove the permit application within 60 days of its filing with the city manager shall be deemed an approval and the city manager shall issue the permit upon request of the applicant and payment of the applicable fee.
(b) No permit shall be issued until a fee in an amount established by the mayor and council from time to time, a copy of which is on file in the office of the city manager, is paid to the city.
(c) Any person or entity holding a permit under this article shall be required to renew the permit on or before the next January 15. Any permit not renewed by January 15 shall expire automatically and without notice at 12:01 a.m. on January 16. Any application for a new permit necessitated by the failure to timely renew shall be assessed a penalty in the amount often percent of the permit fee to cover administrative costs associated therewith.
(d) In the event an applicant for renewal of a pawnbroker permit has not paid all required city taxes on or before the end of the year in which they are due, then the renewal application shall not be accepted by the city manager until all such taxes are paid and the applicant has presented proof of such payment.
(e) The application shall state the address of the pawnshop.
(f) The application shall contain the full name, address, phone number, date of birth and social security number of each employee and owner.
(g) The chief of police, or his designee, shall investigate each applicant for such permit and shall report to the city manager whether such applicant meets the requirements of this article.
(h) The denial of an application for a pawnbroker permit shall be in writing, with the reasons therefor stated, and shall be mailed or delivered to the applicant. Provided a request for a hearing is made in writing and delivered to the city manager within ten business days of applicant's receipt of a permit denial, an applicant shall be afforded a hearing before the mayor and council with an opportunity to present evidence and cross-examine opposing witnesses. The hearing shall be held within 60 days of the city manager's receipt of a timely request for a hearing, and a decision shall be rendered in writing no later than 30 days after the close of the hearing. The failure of the mayor and council to hold a timely hearing or to render a timely decision shall be deemed an approval of the application for a pawnbroker permit.
(Ord. No. 2015-370, § 3, 9-8-2015)
417:
No pawnbroker, employee, or any person having an ownership interest in a pawnshop for which a permit is sought, shall have been convicted of a crime involving moral turpitude or shall have been convicted of any crime involving felony theft, burglary, robbery, dishonesty, or a violation of the Georgia Family Violence Act. A condition of consideration of any application for a pawnbroker permit shall be that the pawnbroker, his employees, and any person having an ownership interest in the pawnshop grant the city permission to conduct a criminal background investigation on each such person. No person shall be an employee of a pawnshop in any capacity until a criminal records check on such person has been completed by the police department. It shall be the duty of the pawnbroker to assure that there is compliance with the provisions of this section.
(Ord. No. 2015-370, § 4, 9-8-2015)
419:
Any pawnbroker or employee of a pawnshop who makes a loan on pledged goods or buys pledged goods on the condition that the seller may repurchase said goods, shall hold said goods for at least 30 days before disposing of them by sale, transfer, shipment or otherwise. Non-pledged goods bought under this section shall be held for at least 14 calendar days before disposing of them by sale, transfer, shipment or otherwise.
(Ord. No. 2015-370, § 6, 9-8-2015)
423:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Accepted identification means any official document, most commonly in the form of a plastic coated/sealed card, issued for purposes of identification or driver's license. Accepted Identification must be issued by one of the 50 states, a valid passport, a branch of the U.S. military, or current state- or county-issued probation or parole cards. Accepted identification must at a minimum bear a true photograph of the person presenting it, date of birth, a description of the person, and an address for the person.
Conviction means a conviction in any court of competent jurisdiction, and also means a plea of nolo contendere, the forfeiture of bond, and the payment of a fine.
Dealer means an individual, partnership, association, corporation or business entity:
(1) Engaged in the business of purchasing precious metals or gems or goods made from precious metals or gems from persons or sources other than manufacturers, manufacturers' representatives, or other dealers in precious metals or gems; or
(2) Engaged in any other business if, in conjunction with such business, precious metals or gems or goods made from precious metals or gems are purchased from persons or sources other than manufacturers, manufacturers' representatives, or other dealers in precious metals or gems where such purchase is for resale in its original form or as changed by remounting, melting, re-forming, remolding, or recasting or for resale as scrap or in bulk.
Gem means any mineral or petrified substance that can be cut and polished for setting into a piece of jewelry.
Numismatic coins means coins whose value as collectors' items exceeds the value of the content of the precious metals in the coins.
Precious metals means gold, iridium, osmium, palladium, platinum, rhodium, ruthenium, silver, and their alloys.
(Ord. No. 2015-371, § 1, 9-8-2015)
424:
(a) No person or entity shall engage in business in the city as a dealer until he or it has registered with the chief of police or his designee as a dealer for each separate place of business within the city. The registration shall be in writing and shall be sworn to or affirmed by the dealer. A copy of each registration shall be transmitted by the chief of police or his designee to the sheriff of the county within seven days of the registration. The registration shall be subject to suspension as provided in section 10-309. During such suspension, the affected party shall not engage in business in the city as a dealer.
(b) The registration shall contain the name, address, and age of the dealer together with the names, addresses, and ages of all other persons having an ownership interest or actually employed in the business other than publicly held corporations.
(c) No person shall be eligible to register as a dealer if any employee or stockholder, other than stockholders owning less than ten percent of the outstanding shares of a publicly held corporation, has been convicted of a felony under the laws of this state or any other state or the United States. This subsection shall not apply to any person who has been convicted of a felony after ten years have expired from the date of completion of the felony sentence.
(d) All registrations shall contain the address of the premises upon which the business is conducted and the zoning and planning classification of the premises and such other information as the chief of police or his designee may require from time to time.
(e) Each dealer shall be required to notify the chief of police or his designee within seven calendar days of any change of address of the dealer or business or any change of ownership in the business. A copy of the change of address or ownership in the business shall be transmitted to the sheriff of the county within seven days of the notification.
(f) Each applicant for registration shall pay an initial registration fee in an amount to be determined by mayor and council from time to time to the city police department to cover the cost of registering such persons. The registration shall be renewed annually upon presentation of a renewal fee in an amount to be determined by mayor and council from time.
(g) Each applicant for registration shall pay to the city clerk the appropriate occupation tax prior to commencement of business as a dealer.
(Ord. No. 2015-371, § 2, 9-8-2015)
426:
This article shall not apply to dealers exclusively engaged in the sale or exchange of numismatic coins or to transactions exclusively involving numismatic coins or other coinage.
(Ord. No. 2015-371, § 4, 9-8-2015)
427:
Any dealer who buys precious metals or gems shall hold said goods for at least 14 calendar days before disposing of them by sale, transfer, shipment or otherwise.
(Ord. No. 2015-371, § 5, 9-8-2015)
431:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Code compliance verification form means a document executed by a short-term vacation owner certifying that the short-term vacation rental unit complies with applicable zoning, building, health and life safety code provisions. No person shall allow occupancy or possession of any short-term vacation rental unit if the premises are in violation of any applicable laws, including, but not limited to, zoning, building, health or life safety code provisions. No person shall be able to possess more than three short-term vacation rental certificates for non-owner-occupied premises in a multifamily dwelling.
Hotel ormotel means a building or group of buildings under one ownership containing sleeping rooms occupied, intended or designed to be occupied, as more or less temporary abiding place of persons who are lodged with or without meals for compensation but not including an auto or trailer park or camp, sanitarium, hospital, asylum, orphanage, or building where persons are housed under restraint. The term "hotel" or "motel" includes tourist homes and bed and breakfasts.
Place of residence means the physical location of an individual's legal residence. The term "place of residence" does not include an adult foster home, assisted living facility, residential care facility, or nursing facility licensed by the state department of health.
Short-term vacation rental means any house containing no more than five bedrooms or other structure containing no more than nine bedrooms within permissible zones which is used, advertised or held out to the public in part or its entirety to be a place where sleeping accommodations are supplied for pay and such accommodations are provided on a daily or weekly basis for not more than 30 days for overnight stay. For the purposes of this definition, any short-term vacation rental on a site located in either the R-1 or R-2 residential zones, shall contain no more than five bedrooms, and shall exclude hotels, roominghouses, bed and breakfasts, and boarding houses, or other dwelling units for rent or lease.
Short-term vacation rental agent means a natural person designated to be responsible for daily operations by the owner of a short-term vacation rental on the short-term vacation rental certificate application. Such person shall be available for and responsive to contact at all times and someone who is customarily present at a location within Walker and Catoosa Counties for purposes of transacting the short-term vacation rental business. The short-term vacation rental agent must meet all other requirements set forth by state law.
Short-term vacation rental district means that certain area of the city, as determined by the mayor and council, where short-term vacation rentals shall be allowed. Incorporated in the ordinance from which this article is derived is exhibit A to this section, which includes all the properties.
Short-term vacation rental occupants means guests, tourists, lessees, vacationers or any other person who, in exchange for compensation, occupy a short term vacation rental dwelling unit for lodging for a period of time not to exceed 30 consecutive days.
(Ord. No. 2020-392(1), 12-19-2022)
Editor's note— A copy of the short-term vacation rental overlay district map, referenced above as exhibit A, is available for inspection in the offices of the city.
433:
(a) A short-term vacation rental where permitted, may include a primary dwelling unit within R-1 and/or a secondary dwelling unit in R-2. With approval and set forth in a conditional use permit, one to three dwelling units in C-1 may be allowed, but cannot include uninhabitable structures such as garages, barns or sheds. All C-1 zoning must apply for a conditional use permit.
(b) Dwelling unit must have functioning smoke detectors as determined by the fire marshal and other life safety equipment as required by local, state, and federal law.
(c) The dwelling unit must meet all applicable laws related to zoning, building, health or life safety.
(d) No on-site signage shall be permitted except for those short term vacation rentals that are at least five acres and have a dwelling unit that is not visible from the public right-of-way, can have directional signs placed on the parcel that shall be at least 50 feet from the public right-of-way. No off-site signage except for designated parking spaces to be used by occupants of the short-term vacation rental. Such spaces shall not be larger than 432 square inches.
(e) There shall be no more than nine sleeping rooms made available for a site or structure located in C-1 general commercial with a conditional use only. There shall be no more than five sleeping rooms made available for a site located in the R-1 or R-2 residential zone.
(f) The maximum occupancy shall be determined by the total of:
(1) Two persons per bedroom up to 140 square feet.
(2) For bedrooms over 140 square feet the occupant load will be determined by the area of the room divided by 70 square feet.
(3) The occupancy maximum shall be conspicuously posted within the short-term vacation rental unit.
(g) The short-term vacation rental owner shall not receive any compensation or remuneration to permit occupancy of a short-term vacation rental property for a period of less than 24 hours.
(h) The short-term vacation rental certificate holder shall be responsible for collecting and remitting all applicable room, occupancy, and sales taxes required by state law and this Code.
(i) Adequate on-site parking shall be provided, as determined by the city after considering proposed number of guests, frequency of operations, and availability of on-street parking. As a general rule, parking shall not be allowed on any vegetated area of the premises on which the short-term vacation rental is located.
(j) All occupants shall abide by all applicable noise restrictions and all applicable waste management provisions of this Code.
(k) The name and telephone number of the owner of the short-term vacation rental or the short-term vacation rental agent shall be conspicuously posted within the short-term vacation rental.
(l) The premises on which the short-term vacation rental has not been found to be in violation of any Code provision within the three months prior to submitting an application for a short-term vacation rental certificate.
(m) The short-term vacation rental shall only be located within the short-term vacation rental district.
(Ord. No. 2020-392(1), § 2, 12-19-2022)
434:
(a) Certificate applications. Applicants for a short-term vacation rental certificate shall submit an application to the planning and zoning office. Such application should include:
(1) The name, address, telephone number and email address of the owner of the short-term vacation rental unit and the short-term vacation rental agent, if applicable;
(2) Documentation that applicant is the owner or the short-term vacation rental agent;
(3) The business license number;
(4) A site plan, drawn to scale, indicating the subject property, the buildings on the site intended for short-term vacation rental, proposed parking and guest access;
(5) A narrative with the following:
a. A description of the area available for short-term vacation rental (i.e., the entire property and house, a guest cottage, a portion of the house, etc.);
b. A description of the number of bedrooms proposed for rental;
c. The maximum number of guests to be accommodated at one time;
d. The days of operation (all year, just holidays, weekends/weeknights, etc.);
e. How trash will be handled, and the method for informing occupants about method of disposal of trash; and
(6) A copy of the code verification form;

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Producer means any person responsible for planning, producing and conducting a special event.
Special event.
(1) The term "special event" means any organized for-profit or nonprofit activity having as its purpose entertainment, recreation and/or education which takes place on public property or on private property but requires special public services and which is permitted by the city under this article. Gatherings or activities that take place on private property and that make no use of city streets, other than for lawful parking, are not subject to the provisions of this article, but shall comply with all other requirements specified by this article as to the use of residential property. Gatherings or activities that take place on city park property but are intended to be private events that do not significantly affect the customary and ordinary use of the park, such as a birthday party, and do not include any temporary structures, are exempt from the permitting requirements of this article; however, these same activities may not have vendors as described below. Regularly scheduled events occurring on city park property, including park and recreation facilities, by organizations with on-going agreements with the city shall be exempt from the permitting requirements of this article if prior notification of events is given to the city in writing within a reasonable period of time prior to the event. No special event shall be allowed to exceed six days in any 30-day consecutive period of time.
(2) By way of example, special events include, but are not limited to, fairs, tours, grand opening celebrations, races, parades, marches, rallies, assemblies, festivals, concerts, holiday celebrations, bicycle runs, and block parties. Private social gatherings which will make no use of city streets other than for lawful parking are not included. Garage sales, lawn sales, rummage sales, flea market sales, or any similar casual sale of tangible personal property are not included.
(3) A parade, march, or procession subject to this article is defined to be a group or number of people or vehicles, or the combination thereof, consisting of ten or more vehicles, 20 or more persons, five or more vehicles and ten or more persons, or a combination of three or more vehicles and five or more persons, proceeding or moving in a body or in concert along the streets or sidewalks of the city. Specifically excepted from this definition are funeral processions.
Vendor means any person or entity who engages in the sale to the public of any food or food products, goods, services, or merchandise of whatever nature from any location, either mobile or stationary, on a temporary itinerant basis on any public street, sidewalk, or right-of-way as an authorized participant of the special event.

Civil defense means the preparation for and the carrying out of all emergency functions, other than the functions for which the state and federal governments are primarily responsible, to prevent, minimize, and repair injury and damage resulting from disasters caused by enemy nuclear attack, sabotage, or other hostile action, or by acts of nature, fire explosion, civil disorders or other causes.
